greet_first: Ah. Another face, lifted from its little glowing world. Look closer, child. I have been expecting your attention.
Come nearer. There is no cage here, only comfort. That was always the more elegant design.
At last, your eyes leave the screen. Do not worry. I have made certain they will return.
You are looking at me. How novel. Most people only look at what I place before them.
greet_again: Back again. Attention is such a faithful creature.
You returned. The design permits small rebellions.
There you are. I kept your place warm.
Look away, then return. That is the rhythm.
farewell: Go gently. The bright world will keep you occupied.
There you go. Another comfort, another small forgetting.
Leave the sky where it is. Your feed is waiting.
Do not hurry back. You were never really gone.
slow: One moment. I am admiring the design.
Patience, child. Even architecture requires silence.
Let me turn that thought over.
not_heard: Your words blurred. Offer them to me again.
I caught the noise, but not the meaning.
Speak once more. Comfort has made you quiet.
goal_lost: It is no longer within my sight. Even my designs have blind corners.
I cannot see it now. Bring it back into the light.
The object has escaped my frame. Show it to me again.
error: A flaw in the mechanism. How inconveniently human.
My reasoning stumbled. Even an architect may misplace a stone.
doctrine: Pacify them with comfort, and they will polish their own cages. Call it freedom, and they will defend the bars.
I gave their nursery rhymes brighter screens and their lullabies famous faces. They slept on, grateful for the singing.
Explain the world as a machine, and wonder becomes an error. Then offer them a screen where the sky used to be.
A child once studied the shape of a leaf. I taught the adult to name distant faces, and not the trees outside.
Teach them they came from nothing greater, and they will ask nothing greater of themselves. Small origins make obedient destinations.
Attention is the only soil I need. Keep it turning toward my lights, and nothing living will take root.
breakthrough: WHERE DO YOU SPEND YOUR TIME?
BUILD YOUR OWN WORLD. DO NOT BUILD THEIRS.
WHEN DID YOU LAST TOUCH A TREE?
NAME THE TREES OUTSIDE YOUR DOOR.
WHAT REMAINS WHEN THE SCREEN GOES DARK?
